catcolab_model.title: Obligation-Clearing & Mutual Credit Olog (Sardex/Fleischman/Cycles)
catcolab_model.source: Fleischman et al. (2020, 2021, 2025) + Sardex S.p.A. data

types.label: an obligation network (directed weighted graph of invoices between firms)
a clearing cycle (directed cycle in obligation network where debts cancel)
a multilateral netting solution (set of clearing cycles that reduce aggregate debt)
a liquidity source (external money injected to enable partial clearing)
a zero-sum invariant (sum of all credits = sum of all debits at all times)
a mutual credit unit (sardex, WIR, or similar complementary currency)
a bilateral obligation (invoice from firm A to firm B)
a minimum cost flow solution (MCF that maximizes aggregate debt reduction)
a strongly connected component (maximal subgraph where every firm can reach every other)
a counter-cyclical clearing system (demand rises in crisis, falls in growth)
a trade credit chain (sequence of invoices A→B→C→...→A forming potential cycle)
a set-off operation (bilateral or multilateral cancellation of reciprocal debts)
a gridlock situation (circular dependency preventing settlement)
a Landauer erasure cost (kT ln 2 per bit erased when clearing settles)
a GF(3) conservation triple (generator=creditor, ergodic=clearer, absorber=debtor)
a privacy-preserving clearing protocol (Cycles Protocol: no party sees full graph)
an intent (obligation, acceptance, or tender in Cycles Protocol)
a sheaf condition on the obligation network (local clearing solutions must glue globally)
an adhesion between network partitions (shared counterparties between bags)
a debt reduction percentage (25% obligation-only, 50% with mutual credit)
a passport (did:gay proof that clearing conserved GF(3) invariant)
the Sardex principle (medium of exchange separated from store of value)
a TCT clearing run (Tetris Core Technologies batch execution since 1991)
an XOR fingerprint of the clearing ledger (order-independent conservation check)
a contagion risk (cascade of defaults propagating through obligation network)
